script.title: Movement vs Shift of Demand Curve
script.caption_hook: Slide along the demand curve or shift it? Check the cause first.

lines.say: Demand curve: do I slide along it or shift it?
Ask one thing first: what caused the change? The cause decides whether we slide or shift.
So the cause matters more than the graph?
If only the good's own price changes, we slide along the same curve. Any other factor moves the whole curve.
Like when a samosa drops from ₹20 to ₹15?
Yes. Cheaper samosas, more bought, same curve. We slide down: extension of demand. A price rise gives contraction.
And if my pocket money rises instead?
Then the curve shifts. Income, tastes, related goods' prices, expectations, number of buyers: all shift it.
Oh! More demand at every price means shift right?
Yes, right shift is increase in demand, left is decrease. For an inferior good, higher income shifts it left.
If tea gets costlier, what happens to coffee demand?
Tea is a substitute, so coffee sells more at every price. Coffee's curve shifts right: increase in demand.
